prompt.context: Your client is a U.S. state's social services agency. The agency is responsible for administering the state's social work programs. Recently, the state legislature passed a law that will change the agency's funding structure. Previously, the agency had been funded at a fixed dollar amount. Now, under the new law, the agency will be paid according to performance, as measured by the number of interviews they conduct with state social work clients.
prompt.question: The agency has hired you to determine how the change will affect them and what they should do about it.

clarifying_info.q: What activities does the agency perform?
clarifying_info.a: For the purpose of simplicity, the agency's only activity is conducting interviews.

clarifying_info.q: How was the agency previously funded?
clarifying_info.a: Previously, the agency received $50,000 per employee per year.

clarifying_info.q: How much of that cost went to salary vs. overhead?
clarifying_info.a: On average $30,000 went to salary and $20,000 went to overhead.

clarifying_info.q: How many employees does the agency have?
clarifying_info.a: Unknown. This case is on a per-employee basis.

clarifying_info.q: How will the agency now be funded?
clarifying_info.a: The agency will be paid $25 per interview.

clarifying_info.q: How many interviews does each social worker conduct per day?
clarifying_info.a: Currently each social worker conducts an average of 5 interviews per day.

clarifying_info.q: How long does it currently take to conduct an interview?
clarifying_info.a: It takes one hour: 40 minutes is the interview itself and 20 minutes is follow-up data entry.

clarifying_info.q: Can the agency increase the number of interviews per social worker per day?
clarifying_info.a: Under the current system, the agency could boost the number of interviews from 5 to 6 per day.

clarifying_info.q: Is there any way to reduce the 20 minutes of data entry time?
clarifying_info.a: The agency has found a very inexpensive transcription software program that would allow them to cut the 20 minutes to 10.

clarifying_info.q: Can the agency obtain additional funding from private or charitable sources?
clarifying_info.a: The agency can garner $1,000 per employee per year from a private charitable trust.

clarifying_info.q: Can the agency reduce overhead by sharing facilities with other state agencies?
clarifying_info.a: Yes, the agency can consolidate its offices into other state agency buildings at a savings of $4,000 per employee per year.

clarifying_info.q: Are all social workers paid evenly?
clarifying_info.a: No. 30% are paid $25K/year, 40% are paid $30K/year, and 30% are paid $35K/year. The agency can convert half of the workers at the highest pay grade to the lowest pay grade.

framework: Understand the previous funding structure (fixed $50,000 per employee per year: $30K salary + $20K overhead)
Understand the new funding structure (performance-based: $25 per interview conducted)
Quantify the budget shortfall under the new structure assuming current operations
Identify revenue-side levers to close the gap (more interviews per day, additional funding sources)
Identify cost-side levers to close the gap (reduce overhead, restructure salaries)
Synthesize recommendations and quantify each lever's contribution to closing the gap

questions.prompt: Calculate the revenue per employee per year under the new funding structure, assuming current operations (5 interviews/day). What is the budget shortfall?
questions.guidance: A strong candidate multiplies work days by interview rate by per-interview payment, then compares to the $50,000 previous funding to surface the shortfall.

math.setup: 250 work days/year × 5 interviews/day × $25/interview versus previous funding of $50,000/employee/year
math.answer: $18,750 per employee per year budget shortfall

questions.prompt: The agency can increase daily interviews from 5 to 6 without any technology changes. How does this affect the shortfall?
questions.guidance: Candidate recalculates annual revenue at 6 interviews/day and finds the remaining gap.

steps: New shortfall = $50,000 − $37,500 = $12,500 per employee per year
math.answer: Shortfall reduced to $12,500 per employee per year

questions.prompt: A transcription software can cut data-entry time from 20 minutes to 10 minutes per interview (interview itself remains 40 minutes). How many interviews per day can a worker now conduct, and what is the new shortfall?
questions.guidance: Candidate calculates time saved per interview, converts to additional interviews per day, recalculates revenue, and finds the remaining gap.

math.setup: Time saved per interview = 10 min; with 6 interviews/day baseline, total time saved = 60 min = 1 additional interview
math.answer: Shortfall reduced to $6,250 per employee per year

questions.prompt: The agency can secure $1,000 per employee per year from a private charitable trust. What is the remaining shortfall?
questions.guidance: Straightforward subtraction; candidate should note this is a revenue-side lever.

math.answer: Shortfall reduced to $5,250 per employee per year

questions.prompt: The agency can consolidate offices into other state agency buildings, saving $4,000 per employee per year in overhead. What is the remaining shortfall?
questions.guidance: Candidate applies the cost-side lever; shortfall shrinks significantly.

math.answer: Shortfall reduced to $1,250 per employee per year

questions.prompt: Salary structure: 30% earn $25K, 40% earn $30K, 30% earn $35K. The agency can convert half of the highest-paid workers (30%) to the lowest pay grade ($25K). What are the per-employee savings, and does this close the gap?
questions.guidance: Candidate computes the weighted salary saving per employee and checks whether the gap is fully closed.

math.setup: Half of the 30% at $35K are moved to $25K. New distribution: 45% at $25K, 40% at $30K, 15% at $35K. Saving = 15% × ($35K − $25K)
steps: Net position = −$1,250 + $1,500 = +$250 per employee per year (surplus)
math.answer: $1,500 in salary savings per employee per year; the agency ends up with a $250 surplus per employee per year, which can help offset the cost of the new transcription software

brainstorming.prompt: What are the ways the agency could close the funding gap?

categories.name: Increase revenue — more interviews
ideas: Increase daily interviews from 5 to 6 through better scheduling
Adopt transcription software to cut data-entry time and add a 7th daily interview

categories.name: Increase revenue — additional funding
ideas: Seek federal grants or supplemental state appropriations
Partner with nonprofits for co-funding arrangements

categories.name: Reduce overhead costs
ideas: Consolidate offices into other state agency buildings ($4,000/employee/year savings)
Reduce utility and facilities spending through shared services
Renegotiate vendor contracts for IT and supplies

categories.name: Reduce salary costs
ideas: Convert half of highest-paid workers to lowest pay grade ($1,500/employee/year savings)
Implement a hiring freeze and rely on attrition
Introduce performance-based pay aligned with interview volumes

recommendation: The funding change will create an $18,750 per employee per year budget shortfall if the agency continues current operations

To close the gap, the agency should implement a combination of revenue increases and cost reductions: (1) boost daily interviews to 6 through scheduling improvements, (2) deploy transcription software to enable 7 interviews per day — adding $12,500/employee/year in revenue vs. baseline, (3) secure $1,000/employee/year from a private charitable trust, (4) consolidate offices with other state agencies saving $4,000/employee/year, and (5) restructure the salary mix saving $1,500/employee/year
Together these measures yield a $250 per employee per year net surplus, which can offset the cost of the transcription software investment
risks: Increasing interview volume per day could reduce interview quality or client outcomes, undermining the program's social mission
Salary restructuring may cause attrition among high-performing senior workers
Charitable trust funding is not guaranteed year-over-year and introduces revenue volatility
Office consolidation may reduce geographic accessibility for clients
next_steps: Evaluate the cost and implementation timeline for the transcription software
Negotiate the office-sharing arrangement with other state agencies
Engage the private charitable trust to secure a multi-year funding commitment
Monitor interview quality metrics after productivity improvements to ensure client outcomes are maintained
